high_level_description: Wordless hand-sewn textile-appliqué illustration of Dunkirk carnival volunteers repairing a Reuze wicker giant from an approved jig, independently testing every joint, retaining physical proof samples, and keeping the parade threshold closed until human validation; constructed entirely from clet’che fabrics, wicker, painted cloth and bold popular-print silhouettes.

compositional_deconstruction.background: One flat field of natural sailcloth fills the page, pieced with irregular areas of navy-and-cream sailor stripes, magenta faux fur, yellow oilskin, emerald satin, red cotton, black felt, and visible hand stitching. Materials meet as one shallow appliqué surface without realistic workshop, floor, sky, street, photographic light, modeled depth, perspective recession, decorative cultural border, writing, letter, numeral, caption, arrow, diagram connector, progress bar, interface, factory conveyor, national flag, crown, podium, throne, certification seal, ranking device, watermark, or historical photograph.

elements.desc: Approved full-scale wicker construction jig occupying the upper-left field, shaped as the exact profile of the giant’s head and shoulders. Five distinct curved sockets define the permitted repair joints through physical contours alone; four hold completed sample weaves and the fifth remains empty, with no measurement text, numeral, arrow, checklist, signature, seal, screen, or authority emblem.

Dunkirk Reuze carnival giant under repair, built from ochre woven wicker with a painted cloth face, black felt hair, red jacket, cream ruff, and navy sash. Four structural splices are tightly finished while one shoulder opening remains accessible for the current matching weave; the coherent figure has no royal crown, supernatural aura, written name, badge, or mechanical interior.

Adult Dunkirk carnival volunteer acting as the repair driver, light-brown skin, short black curls, bright cheek paint, navy-and-cream striped shirt, magenta faux-fur work apron, emerald trousers, and black shoes. Kneeling beside the open shoulder, they fit one pre-shaped wicker strip into the final permitted joint while every other body area remains untouched and no tool grants wider authority.

Adult Dunkirk carnival craft volunteer performing verification, dark-brown skin, long dark braid, yellow oilskin jacket over a red-and-white striped shirt, cobalt trousers, and green shoes. They pull a plain tension strap across one completed wicker splice using both hands, comparing its flex with a fixed wooden arc gauge while remaining separate from the repair driver and final closure control.

Older Dunkirk carnival volunteer serving as independent reviewer at equal scale, medium-brown skin, short wavy gray hair, violet cheek paint, emerald coat with cream faux-fur collar, striped trousers, and red shoes. They compare the repaired shoulder with the approved jig using a matching curved gauge; one hand holds the gauge while the other stays away from the closed threshold latch.

Low wicker proof chest containing the featured repair evidence as one unified object: four paired splice samples already tension-bent without breaking, one empty fitted recess awaiting the final sample, the removed damaged strand, and matching pigment and cloth swatches. Every compartment is shape-specific and unlabeled, with no certificate, score, letter, number, glowing status, lock of office, or monetary token.

Freestanding parade threshold at the upper-right edge, made from black timber wrapped in navy striped cloth and topped by three closed carnival umbrellas in magenta, yellow, and green. Five differently shaped wooden latches span its closed opening; four align with retained proof samples while the fifth remains engaged, physically preventing release before the reviewer completes the final check.
